Adds Sec 5.4 cross-asset robustness (QQQ/IWM/TLT/GLD), executed 2026-09-17 against a v2 fallback dataset after the true v1 raw payload for these four symbols was confirmed unrecoverable (owner decision). SPY v1 primary result (Sec 5.1-5.3) is unchanged and stays the sole primary consumed result -- the robustness result is pre-specified robustness / post-primary characterization, never a substitute for it. Adds two new metrics not previously surfaced: adverse (intra-horizon peak-to-trough) drawdown, and moving-block/stationary block-bootstrap uncertainty on regime-conditional mean returns (150 resamples, 90% CI) -- both implemented in financial_dynamics.backtesting.metrics this session, covered by 11 new unit tests (320 total pass). Dataset provenance disclosed plainly: v2 does NOT hash-match the frozen v1 manifest for SPY/QQQ/IWM/TLT (GLD alone matches -- it pays no distributions, so its raw-close series is bit-reproducible; the others carry dividend adjustment, which is not); this pattern is consistent with dividend-adjustment recomputation drift but the cause is NOT claimed as proven -- see data/manifests/yf_fd_etfs_daily_2015_2025_v2_PROVENANCE.md. Cross-symbol pattern reported factually: CALM_TREND absent from the 2025 holdout in QQQ/IWM/TLT (matching SPY), present in GLD; QQQ/IWM negative mean_return_h1 in 2025 holdout (matching SPY sign), TLT/GLD positive -- reported as a pattern, not asserted as statistically significant or causally explained. Updates Sec 7 Limitations to reflect what is now available (robustness metrics/bootstrap) vs. what remains a gap for SPY v1 specifically (no re-run of an already-consumed primary result).
